L220: L221: The Company's Services L222: The Company offers a full range of security services, consisting of: L223: (i) consulting and planning; (ii) engineering and design; (iii) systems L224: integration; and (iv) maintenance and technical support. At the beginning of L225: each new client relationship, the Company designates one of its professional L226: staff as the client service contact. This individual is the focal point for L227: communications between the Company and the client and often acts as the client's L228: project manager for all of its security needs. The Company's engagement may L229: include one or more of the elements described below. L230: Consulting and Planning. Security consulting and planning are the L231: initial phases of determining a security solution for a project. The Company has L232: developed a planning process that identifies all systems, policies and L233: procedures that are required for the successful operation of a security system L234: that will both meet a client's current needs and accommodate its projected L235: future requirements. The Company's consulting and planning process includes the L236: following steps: L237: Identify the client's objectives and security system requirements L238: Review the existing security system plan L239: Survey the site, including inventory of physical components and software L240: and evaluation of client's existing infrastructure and security L241: system L242: Identify and prioritize the client's vulnerabilities L243: Develop and evaluate system alternatives L244: Recommend a conceptual security plan design L245: Estimate the cost of implementing the conceptual plan L246: Develop a preliminary implementation schedule L247: As a result of this process, the Company provides the client with a L248: master plan for security services which recommends an effective security L249: solution that addresses routine operating needs as well as emergency situations. L250: The Company believes that its comprehensive planning process enables its clients L251: to budget for their security requirements on a long-term basis, identify L252: opportunities for cost reduction and prepare for future risks. L253: Engineering and Design. The engineering and design process involves L254: preparation of detailed project specifications and working drawings by a team of L255: the Company's engineers, systems designers and computer-aided design system L256: operators. These specifications and drawings detail the instrument sensitivity L257: requirements, layout of the control center, placement of equipment and L258: electrical requirements. Throughout the engineering and design process, the L259: Company utilizes its expertise in advanced technologies and its understanding of L260: its client's operational preferences to design a system that is functional, L261: cost-effective and accommodates the client's present and future requirements. In L262: addition, the Company attempts to incorporate its client's existing personnel, L263: equipment and other physical resources into the system design. L264: L265: L266: When retained as a single-source provider for turnkey security L267: solutions, the Company also selects the system components required under the L268: specifications and drawings it has prepared. To the extent possible, the Company L269: uses off-the-shelf equipment to minimize the cost of developing custom L270: equipment. The Company has made a strategic decision not to represent any L271: equipment manufacturer exclusively, thereby maintaining objectivity and L272: flexibility in equipment selection. The Company believes that its technical L273: proficiency with the products of a wide range of manufacturers enables it to L274: select components that will best meet a project's requirements. L275: Systems Integration. Systems integration involves (i) equipment L276: procurement; (ii) custom systems modeling and fabrication; (iii) facility L277: installation; (iv) hardware, software and network integration; and (v) system L278: validation and testing. In addition to these basic integration services, the L279: Company provides engineering services to enhance the compatibility of the L280: client's subsystems. The Company prepares technical documentation of the system L281: and operations manuals and provides on-site training to client personnel. L282: Under the supervision of a project manager, the Company's technicians L283: conduct hardware installation, hardware and software integration, system L284: validation and testing. The aspects of systems integration that do not require a L285: high level of technical expertise, such as wire installation and basic L286: construction, are typically performed by the Company's subcontractors. L287: Maintenance and Technical Support. The Company provides maintenance and L288: technical support services on a scheduled, on-call, or emergency basis. These L289: services include developing and implementing maintenance programs both for L290: security systems designed, engineered, or integrated by the Company and for L291: existing systems. L292: Maintenance services offered by the Company include its EMS, a database L293: used by the Company to effectively manage a security system's components, L294: maintenance planning and scheduling, and costs. The system configuration L295: function monitors system activity and capacity, and identifies the need to L296: reconfigure or expand the system. The system maintenance function schedules and L297: records maintenance activity, and identifies equipment replacement and upgrading L298: requirements. L299: L300: Marketing L301: The Company's marketing activities are conducted on both national and L302: regional levels. The Company obtains engagements through direct negotiation with L303: clients, competitive bid processes and referrals. At the national level, the L304: Company conducts analyses of various industries and targets those with L305: significant potential demand for security solutions. At a regional level, under L306: the supervision of senior management, each office develops and implements a L307: marketing plan for its region. The plan identifies prospective clients within L308: the region and sets forth a strategy for developing relationships with them. L309: Each regional office works with the headquarters office in expanding L310: relationships with existing national clients to include facilities within the L311: region. L572: L573: Overview L574: The Company is a single-source provider of comprehensive, L575: technology-based security solutions for medium and large commercial and L576: government facilities in the United States and abroad. The Company offers a L577: broad range of services, including: (i) consulting and planning; (ii) L578: engineering and design; (iii) systems integration; and (iv) maintenance and L579: technical support. L580: The Company began operations in 1987 in association with a large L581: privately held engineering firm. As a start-up, the Company expended significant L582: capital on the development of the Company's business and infrastructure, and it L583: accumulated losses of approximately $2.8 million from 1987 through 1991 on L584: aggregate revenues of approximately $17.2 million. The Company's revenues from L585: 1990 through 1994 were generated primarily by a contract to design and integrate L586: extensive security upgrades at three nuclear facilities for the Tennessee Valley L587: Authority (the "TVA"). In 1992, the Company became independent from the L588: engineering firm in conjunction with a capital infusion from a private investor L589: group. At the same time, the Company hired new management with extensive L590: expertise in the security industry. Since 1992, the Company has devoted a L591: substantial amount of resources and capital to enhancing its technical L592: capability and services offerings, hiring and training key personnel and L593: expanding its client base. As part of this effort, the Company opened four L594: regional offices in the United States. In November 2000, the Company acquired L595: SSI, a Security Systems Integration firm exclusively providing security systems L596: and services to the U.S. Government. The resources and contracts of SSI were L597: merged with those of the Company and became the Government Division of the L598: Company. The merger of SSI increased the yearly revenue of the Company by 40%. L599: The Company derives its revenue primarily from long-term, fixed-price L600: contracts. Earnings are recognized based upon the Company's estimates of the L601: cost and percentage of completion of individual contracts. Earned revenue equal L602: the project's total contract amount multiplied by the proportion that direct L603: project costs incurred on a project bear to estimated total project costs. L604: Project costs include direct labor and benefits, direct material, subcontract L605: costs, project related travel and other direct expenses. L606: Clients are invoiced based upon negotiated payment terms for each L607: individual contract. Terms usually include a 25% down payment and the balance as L608: stages of the work are completed. Maintenance contracts are billed either in L609: advance, monthly, or quarterly. As a result, the Company records as an asset, L610: costs and estimated earnings in excess of billings and as a liability, billings L611: in excess of costs and estimated earnings.
